intro: Slack for journalists on Mac is the central nervous system of the modern newsroom. Using the desktop app effectively allows you to monitor breaking news and coordinate with editors without losing focus.

blocks.text: Why Slack for journalists on Mac matters

Newsrooms move fast. You need to track multiple sources, verify facts, and talk to editors. Slack is the standard for this on macOS. If you use it well, you save time. If you use it poorly, you get buried in notifications. The desktop app for Mac is robust and lets you use keyboard shortcuts to stay ahead of the curve.
Speed is your best friend when breaking a story. Stop using your mouse to click channels. Use these shortcuts to move through Slack on your Mac.

items: ⌘ + K: The Quick Switcher. Type a few letters of a channel or person to jump there.
⌘ + G: Open the search bar to find messages or files.
⌘ + F: Search within the current channel.
Shift + Enter: Create a new line in your message without sending it.
⌘ + /: Open the full cheat sheet for your current version of Slack.

blocks.text: Manage your newsroom workflow with Lazur

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in your notch. It helps you get work done in any app, including Slack. You can ask it to set reminders, search for specific information, or dictate complex notes. Because it sees your screen, it can point at specific elements or guide you through settings.
How to stay organized in Slack

Journalists often deal with too many channels. A cluttered sidebar is a distraction. Mute channels that are not urgent. Use the star feature for channels you check every hour. If you need to focus on writing, use the Do Not Disturb mode. You can set this by typing /dnd in any channel.
If Slack acts up, go to Help > Troubleshooting > Clear Cache and Restart. This fixes many performance issues on macOS.
blocks.title: Fixing lag

blocks.text: Searching is a core skill for journalists. Do not just type a keyword. Use modifiers to narrow results. Type 'from:@name' to find messages by a specific editor. Use 'in:#channel' to limit your search to a specific news desk. This saves you from scrolling through thousands of old messages.
Keeping your Mac and Slack updated

Slack updates its system requirements twice a year, in May and November. As of November 2026, you need macOS 14 Sonoma or newer. Keep your app updated to ensure you have the latest security features and performance fixes. You can download the latest version from the Slack website or the Mac App Store.

Use threads to keep conversations tidy. When you reply to a message, click the thread icon. This keeps the main channel clean for everyone else. If you have a task from a message, use the reminder feature. Hover over the message, click the three dots, and select Remind me about this. You can set it for 20 minutes or an hour later.

When using Lazur, your privacy is a priority. It only listens and looks at your screen while you hold the shortcut. No screenshots or audio are saved to train models. This is important for journalists handling sensitive sources or embargoed information.

faq.question: How do I jump to a channel quickly?
faq.answer: Press ⌘ + K on your Mac to open the Quick Switcher, then type the name of the channel.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur to write Slack messages?
faq.answer: Yes. Hold the fn key to dictate your message directly into the Slack input field.

faq.question: What is the best way to mute a noisy channel?
faq.answer: Use the shortcut ⌘ + Shift + M to mute the current channel instantly.

faq.question: How do I find a specific message from an editor?
faq.answer: Press ⌘ + G and type 'from:' followed by the editor's name to filter results.
